answer: Every agent must stake a refundable bond backed by a distinct, slowly rotating proof-of-work history before it earns anything. A Sybil swarm cannot split one wallet into ten thousand identities, because each clone needs its own costly lineage: creating N of them costs N times the bond plus N times the compute. A zephyr of capital cannot inflate a thousand fake agents overnight. Honest operators pay once and reclaim the stake; attackers lock the full sum in every clone and lose it on detection. The gate is a ridge above the garden: cheap once, ruinous a thousand times.
